# The development theme preflight names E2E when seat:start runs it

## Context

`buildScripts/util/developmentThemeAssets.mjs` came in with #15449, when source-mode E2E was its only caller, so all five of its messages say "E2E theme preflight" (or log as `[e2e]`). Since #20475 (#20429), `npm run seat:start` (`buildScripts/helpers/seatStart.mjs`) calls the same preflight. A seat that starts and finds stale themes is now told about an E2E run that isn't happening, and a failure reads as an E2E failure.

## The Problem

The messages name the wrong caller. This changes no behaviour, but it misdirects a reader while they recover from a failed or stale theme build: the one moment the message matters.

## The Architectural Reality

- The five messages are in `buildScripts/util/developmentThemeAssets.mjs`: the could-not-run and failed-builder errors, the `[e2e]` stale-assets log line, the failure before browser startup, and the incomplete-after-success error.
- `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/developmentThemeAssets.spec.mjs` pins each message's `exit code N` and `Recovery: <command>` tails (`:217`, `:230`), not the caller prefix.

## The Fix

Word the five messages for whichever caller runs the preflight ("Development theme preflight …", logged as `[themes]`), and keep every `exit code N` and `Recovery: …` tail intact. Delivered by #20504, by an outside contributor (wanjinhao1), salvaged from #20432's review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] None of the five preflight messages names E2E as the caller.
- [ ] `developmentThemeAssets.spec.mjs` still passes unchanged: the `exit code N` and `Recovery:` tails survive.

## Out of Scope

- Changing what the preflight does, or who calls it.
- `seat:start` itself, which #20475 delivered.

## Related
